key_insight: LLMs can sound clinically competent, but their diagnostic reasoning is not consistently structured across similar cases.
clinical_relevance: For medical AI, final-answer accuracy alone is not enough; process-level reasoning evaluation may better reveal when a model is truly grounded in clinical schemas.
method: Extracted diagnostic traces into clinical reasoning graphs using a domain ontology with 5 node types and 7 edge types.
Analyzed 750 traces from 5 LLMs on 50 NEJM Clinicopathological Conference cases under 3 prompt conditions.
Compared graph similarity for clinically similar versus dissimilar cases, plus correctness-based pairings and component-level signals.
evidence_signal: Across 15 model-condition comparisons, within-cluster and between-cluster similarity were nearly identical, and structured reflection raised explicit feature analysis by 33% without improving cross-case consistency.
watch_item: Graph-based reasoning scores may depend on ontology design and extraction quality, so results should be validated before use in high-stakes model assessment.
paper_title: Clinical Reasoning Graphs: Structured Evaluation of LLM Diagnostic Reasoning Reveals Competence Without Consistency
